physical_vs_commercial_imports.question: Compare Germany's net physical imports with its net scheduled commercial imports last week.

installed_solar_vs_2030_target.question: How much solar capacity is installed in Germany, and what is the 2030 target?

The legal 2030 target under EEG 2023 is 215 GW (AC), which is 94.0 GW more than the current figure. The November 2026 value is for a month still in progress (today is 14 November 2026), so it may be provisional. For reference, the EEG interim target for end-2026 was 128 GW.

solar_market_value_october.question: What was the market value (capture price) of solar power in October 2026, and how does it compare with the official value?

input.a_label: Solar capture price from Energy-Charts data, Oct 2026
input.b_label: Official solar market value (netztransparenz.de), Oct 2026, reported

content.text:
The solar capture price in October 2026 was 13.45 ct/kWh (134.49 EUR/MWh), calculated from Energy-Charts solar generation weighted against day-ahead prices. The official solar market value for the same month is 13.39 ct/kWh, so my figure is 0.06 ct/kWh (0.44%) higher. The official figure is "reported" status (published 10 Nov 2026), not final. The small gap is expected because the official value uses the TSOs' extrapolated feed-in, while mine uses Energy-Charts generation data. The capture rate was 79.45% of the average spot price of 16.93 ct/kWh (169.27 EUR/MWh).

Period: 1–31 October 2026, German local time, public net generation for solar.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE); Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de (day-ahead prices via Energy-Charts.info); official value: netztransparenz.de (German TSOs), as reported by pv magazine/Solarserver.

co2_factor_2025.question: What was the CO2 intensity of German electricity in 2025?

The UBA defines it as direct CO2 emissions from German generation divided by electricity consumed in Germany, excluding emissions caused abroad by net imports.

Source: Umweltbundesamt (UBA), Climate Change 16/2026, published 2026-03-23.

content.text:
The solar capture price for October 2026 was 13.449 ct/kWh in my calculation, against an official solar market value of 13.39 ct/kWh. That is a difference of +0.059 ct/kWh (+0.4%).

wind_speed_last_week.question: How windy was it in Germany last week?

content.text:
Last week (Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026) was a calm week in Germany. The average station wind speed was 3.34 m/s, and the windiest day was Wednesday 4 November (4.78 m/s). The highest hourly mean was 5.64 m/s at 13:00 on 4 November, and only 12 of 168 hours exceeded 5 m/s (my threshold for "windy"). Daily means ranged from 2.31 m/s on 8 November to 4.78 m/s on 4 November.

These values come from 65 DWD weather stations measured about 10 m above ground. They indicate how windy it was, but they are not the wind speeds at turbine hub height (100–150 m), so they do not show what turbines received.

Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), opendata.dwd.de (CC BY 4.0)

price_calm_vs_windy_october.question: In October 2026, how did the day-ahead price in hours with little wind compare with windy hours?

input.b_label: mean day-ahead price, hours with wind above 5 m/s, Oct 2026

content.text:
In October 2026, hours with little wind (station wind below 3 m/s) had a mean day-ahead price of 214.84 EUR/MWh (21.484 ct/kWh). Windy hours (above 5 m/s) averaged 62.61 EUR/MWh (6.261 ct/kWh), a difference of 152.23 EUR/MWh. The month's overall mean was 169.27 EUR/MWh.

These are simple means of hourly prices, with hours that fall in neither category excluded. The wind thresholds are my assumptions, not official definitions. Station wind is measured about 10 m above ground at 65 DWD stations, so it is an indicator of how windy it was, not what turbines received. The results show an association only; demand, gas prices and imports also affect prices.

Period: 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31 (German local time). Hours counted: 304 with little wind and 144 with windy conditions, out of 745.

Source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (day-ahead prices); Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) via opendata.dwd.de (wind speed).

price_germany_vs_france_last_week.question: Was electricity cheaper in France or in Germany last week?

content.text:
On average, France was slightly cheaper than Germany last week. From Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026, the simple average day-ahead price was 256.59 EUR/MWh in Germany and 255.83 EUR/MWh in France, a difference of 0.76 EUR/MWh (0.3%). Germany was more expensive in 39.5 of the 168 hours (counted in 15-minute intervals), so the gap was small and changed direction often.

Source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE). Prices are the Germany-Luxembourg and France day-ahead prices, unweighted averages over all 15-minute intervals.

hours_france_cheaper_last_week.question: In how many hours last week was power cheaper in France than in Germany?

content.text:
In the week of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (Monday to Sunday), France was cheaper than Germany in **47 hours**, or 28.0% of the 168 hours. Counted hourly, Germany was dearer in those hours; the price spread was above zero (Germany minus France). Counted in 15-minute intervals instead, the figure is 158 intervals (39.5 hours), so the two methods differ. The hourly figure is the one to cite. Hours with identical prices are not counted.

Source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE), day-ahead prices for DE-LU and FR.

followup_commercial_imports_from_france.question: How much did Germany import from France in those hours, according to the scheduled commercial exchanges?

content.text:
Last week (Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026), power was cheaper in France than in Germany in **39.5 hours** (158 of 672 quarter-hours, day-ahead prices). In the other hours, Germany was cheaper in 87.0 hours and the prices were equal in 41.5 hours. This counts 15-minute values, so it is not rounded to whole hours.

Source: Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE), day-ahead prices for the Germany-Luxembourg and France zones.

Germany's net scheduled commercial imports from France were **91.22 GWh** in the hours when France was cheaper (1 to 8 November 2026 window: 2–8 November, as in the previous answer).

This uses an hourly comparison, which selected 47 hours, so it differs slightly from the 39.5 hours in my previous answer, which counted 15-minute values. Positive values are net imports into Germany. The energy is the net scheduled exchange, not physical flow.

Source: Energy-Charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE), scheduled commercial exchanges; Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de via Energy-Charts.info (day-ahead prices).

content.text:
Renewable generation curtailed by redispatch in Germany from Monday 2026-11-02 to Sunday 2026-11-08 totalled **1,724 MWh (about 1.72 GWh)**.
